ravi (Finance): Heads up: new hosted billing rules go live July 1, 2026. Main changes: 1) Burst credit pool replaces transient spikes, 2) itemized invoice lines per model+region, 3) trial credit reduced for new signups. Details: https://redwood.internal/docs/billing/2026-update :loudspeaker:

maria (Growth): Does this affect promo credits we run for webinars?

ravi (Finance): Promo credits are unaffected. This change only alters default trial amounts. Promo and partner credits remain as configured per campaign.

jun (Eng): How will clients observe burst usage?

ravi (Finance): Console shows a rolling "Burst remaining" meter and an API endpoint /v1/billing/burst-status. SDKs will get a small update to expose the value.

billing-bot: SAMPLE INVOICE: https://billing.redwood.internal/samples/2026-itemized-sample.pdf (shows per-model, per-region lines and burst usage).

kate (Customer Success): For customers on free trials now, are they grandfathered?

ravi (Finance): Yes, accounts created before July 1 will keep the current trial amount for 45 days, then we show a migration banner. CS will get a CSV of impacted accounts.

maria (Growth): Any pricing changes?

ravi (Finance): No core price changes. We are introducing an optional "burst add-on" SKU for larger immediate pools.

jun (Eng): Will this introduce more 429s?

ravi (Finance): We designed a queue-first grace period for 14 days after rollout; then soft throttles apply. We recommend SDKs implement exponential backoff and idempotency for writes.

kate (Customer Success): Action items: prepare KB, send targeted emails, create migration playbook.

ravi (Finance): Thanks. Questions -> #billing-questions or finance@redwood.com. Exec signoff: Ravinder (CFO). :white_check_mark:
